cards.front: Explain the types of majority used in Parliament, with one constitutional use of each.
cards.back:
TypeMeaningUsed for (examples)
SimpleMore than 50% of members present and voting (Art. 100)Ordinary/Money Bills, no-confidence motion, President’s Rule (356), Financial Emergency (360), election of Speaker
EffectiveMore than 50% of effective strength (total minus vacancies)Removal of Vice-President (Art. 67, in RS), Speaker/Deputy Speaker (Art. 94), Deputy Chairman RS (Art. 90)
AbsoluteMore than 50% of total strength of the HouseNot stand-alone; part of Special Majority Type I (≥272 in LS to form govt)
Special – Type IMajority of total membership + 2/3 of present and votingConstitutional amendment (368), removal of SC/HC judges, CAG, CEC; approval of National Emergency
Special – Type II2/3 of total membership of each HouseImpeachment of the President (Art. 61)
Special – Type III2/3 of present and voting in Rajya Sabha onlyNew All-India Service (Art. 312); Parliament legislating on State List (Art. 249)

cards.front:
Consider the following statements regarding types of majority:

  1. Removal of the Vice-President requires an effective majority in the Rajya Sabha.
  2. Impeachment of the President requires two-thirds of the members present and voting in each House.
  3. Creation of a new All-India Service requires a resolution passed by two-thirds of members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3
cards.back:
Correct Answer: (b) 1 and 3 only

  1. Correct: Art. 67 – effective majority (majority of all the then members) in the Rajya Sabha.
  2. Incorrect: Impeachment (Art. 61) needs two-thirds of the total membership of each House (Special Majority Type II), not of members present and voting.
  3. Correct: Art. 312 – Special Majority Type III in the Rajya Sabha only.

cards.front:
State True or False, with reason:

  1. The oaths of the President and the Governors are given in the Third Schedule.
  2. The CAG’s oath is given in the Third Schedule.
  3. Ministers take both an oath of office and an oath of secrecy.
  4. The 12 nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are allotted under the Fourth Schedule.
cards.back:
Answer

  1. FALSE – They are in Article 60 (President) and Article 159 (Governors).
  2. TRUE – The Third Schedule covers ministers, MPs/MLAs, candidates for election, SC/HC judges and the CAG.
  3. TRUE – The secrecy oath binds ministers not to disclose official matters except as required.
  4. FALSE – The Fourth Schedule allots only elective seats to States/UTs; the 12 nominated seats are outside it.

cards.front: Is the judiciary “State” under Article 12? Name the tests courts use to decide whether a body is an “other authority”.
cards.back:
Judiciary:

  • Rati Lal v. State of Bombay – judiciary is not State.
  • A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak and N.S. Mirajkar – it is State when making rules, but not when exercising judicial power.

Tests for “other authorities”:

  • Instrumentality or agency – Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib (1981)
  • Deep and pervasive State control – Pradeep Kumar Biswas (2002)
  • Public function test

PSUs are not automatically State – only if courts hold so after applying these tests.

cards.front: What are the three elements of Dicey’s Rule of Law? Which of them apply in India?
cards.back:
1. Absence of arbitrary power – no one is punished except for breach of law. Applies.
  2. Equality before law – all are subject to the same laws and ordinary courts. Applies.
  3. Primacy of individual rights – rights flow from court decisions (common law). Does not apply – in India rights come from the Constitution itself.

The Supreme Court has held the Rule of Law to be part of the Basic Structure.

cards.front: Article 14 forbids class legislation but permits reasonable classification. What are the two conditions for a valid classification?
cards.back:
1. Intelligible differentia – a real, substantial distinction between the groups.
  2. Rational nexus – the distinction must relate to the object the law seeks to achieve.

E.g., special laws for women, children and backward classes are valid. Formal equality treats all alike; substantive equality needs positive State action such as reservations.

cards.front: What are the exceptions to equality under Article 14?
cards.back:
ProvisionException
Art. 361President and Governors not answerable to courts for official acts; no criminal case or arrest during term; civil suits for personal acts only after 2 months’ notice
Art. 361ASubstantially true reports of legislative proceedings are protected (not secret sittings or malicious reports)
Arts. 105 and 194MPs/MLAs not liable in court for anything said or any vote given in the House
Art. 31CLaws for Art. 39(b)/(c) cannot be challenged under Art. 14 or 19 (“where 31C comes in, 14 goes out”)
DiplomatsForeign sovereigns and ambassadors are immune (Vienna Convention)
UN agenciesImmunities under the UN (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947

cards.front: What is the present position of the right to property? In which cases is compensation still constitutionally required?
cards.back:
• 44th Amendment (1978) repealed Arts. 19(1)(f) and 31; added Art. 300A (Part XII): “No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.”
  • It is a legal/constitutional right, not a Fundamental Right, and not part of the Basic Structure.
  • Protects against executive action, not legislative action.
  • Remedy through the High Court (Art. 226), not Art. 32.

Compensation still mandatory:

  • Acquisition of property of a minority educational institution (Art. 30(1A)).
  • Land under personal cultivation within the ceiling limit (Art. 31A proviso).

cards.front:
Which of the following are classified as Gandhian principles among the DPSPs?

  1. Promotion of cooperative societies (Art. 43B)
  2. Uniform Civil Code (Art. 44)
  3. Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections (Art. 46)
  4. Separation of judiciary from executive (Art. 50)

Select the correct answer:

(a) 1 and 3 only
(b) 2 and 4 only
(c) 1, 2 and 3 only
(d) 1, 3 and 4 only
cards.back:
Correct Answer: (a) 1 and 3 only

  1. Correct: Art. 43B – Gandhian.
  2. Incorrect: Art. 44 – Liberal-intellectual.
  3. Correct: Art. 46 – Gandhian.
  4. Incorrect: Art. 50 – Liberal-intellectual.

cards.front: Name three directives outside Part IV of the Constitution.
cards.back:
• Art. 335 (Part XVI) – claims of SCs/STs in services, consistent with administrative efficiency.
  • Art. 350A (Part XVII) – instruction in the mother tongue at primary level for linguistic minorities.
  • Art. 351 (Part XVII) – promotion and development of Hindi.

Non-justiciable, but courts read them in harmony with Part IV.

cards.front:
[UPSC 2025] Consider the following pairs:

  1. Separation of Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State — The Directive Principles of State Policy
  2. Valuing and preserving the rich heritage of our composite culture — The Fundamental Duties
  3. Prohibition of employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories — The Fundamental Rights

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) All the three
(d) None
cards.back:
Correct Answer: (c) All the three

  1. Correct: Art. 50 – DPSP.
  2. Correct: Art. 51A(f) – Fundamental Duty.
  3. Correct: Art. 24 – Fundamental Right.
